name: Berlin
localFacts: Settled in 1665 and incorporated in 1812, Berlin is a small open-town-meeting community about 12 miles northeast of Worcester, with a largely rural landscape of farms and wooded lots.
paintingChallenges: Rural lots with heavy tree cover keep siding shaded and damp
Older farmhouses and barns need careful scraping and priming
Well-water homes can show mineral staining on exterior surfaces

name: Blackstone
localFacts: Blackstone sits on the Rhode Island border in the Blackstone River Valley and is part of the Providence metropolitan area, with mill-era village housing alongside newer neighborhoods.
paintingChallenges: Mill-era multi-family homes with many layers of old paint
River valley humidity encourages mildew on shaded siding
Older trim often needs wood repair before repainting

name: Bolton
localFacts: Bolton lies along Interstate 495 about 25 miles west-northwest of Boston. Settled in the 1600s and incorporated in 1738, it is still home to many farms and apple orchards.
paintingChallenges: Large homes on wooded lots need mildew-resistant exterior systems
Barns and outbuildings add to exterior painting scope
Long driveways and setbacks make access planning important

name: Boxborough
localFacts: Boxborough, often written Boxboro on highway signs, is a small Middlesex County town near the meeting point of Interstate 495 and Route 2.
paintingChallenges: Wooded lots keep north-facing siding damp
Larger colonials with extensive trim
Townhouse and condo associations with shared exterior schedules

name: Boylston
localFacts: Boylston is a small Worcester County town on the eastern shore of the Wachusett Reservoir, with a mostly residential and rural character.
paintingChallenges: Reservoir-side humidity encourages mildew
Older farmhouses mixed with newer subdivisions
Shaded lots slow exterior drying times

name: Carlisle
localFacts: Carlisle is a small, largely rural town northwest of Boston in Middlesex County, known for its large-lot zoning, conservation land and open farmland.
paintingChallenges: Large custom homes with extensive exterior trim
Heavy tree cover and long shaded walls
Cedar and wood siding that needs regular maintenance

name: Charlton
localFacts: Charlton is a Worcester County town in south-central Massachusetts, with a mix of rural roads, farmland and growing residential neighborhoods.
paintingChallenges: Mix of older farmhouses and newer subdivisions
Wooded lots that keep siding shaded
Long winters shorten the exterior painting season

name: Clinton
localFacts: Clinton is a compact Worcester County town at the southern end of the Wachusett Reservoir, with a historic downtown and many 19th-century mill-era homes.
paintingChallenges: 19th-century homes often contain lead paint
Multi-family buildings with shared exterior work
Dense downtown lots make access and staging tight

name: Dudley
localFacts: Dudley is a Worcester County town on the Connecticut border in south-central Massachusetts and the home of Nichols College.
paintingChallenges: Older mill village homes with layered paint
Rental and student housing turnovers
Shaded rural lots with mildew growth

name: Foxborough
localFacts: Foxborough, often written Foxboro, sits about 22 miles southwest of Boston and is home to Gillette Stadium.
paintingChallenges: Busy summer schedules around events and traffic
Mix of older center homes and newer subdivisions
Wooded neighborhoods with mildew-prone siding

name: Harvard
localFacts: Harvard is a farming community about 25 miles west-northwest of Boston, settled in 1658 and home to the historic Fruitlands site and Harvard Shaker Village.
paintingChallenges: Historic and antique homes need sensitive prep
Orchard and farm properties with outbuildings
Large wooded lots with long shaded walls

name: Lancaster
localFacts: Incorporated in 1653, Lancaster is the oldest town in Worcester County and includes the village of South Lancaster.
paintingChallenges: Very old homes with original wood siding
Lead paint common on antique exteriors
River and wetland humidity in low-lying areas

name: Lincoln
localFacts: Lincoln is a MetroWest town with a large amount of colonial history and conservation land, including residents of Hanscom Air Force Base within town limits.
paintingChallenges: Historic homes and modernist houses need different approaches
Wood siding surrounded by conservation woodland
Large properties with significant trim and windows

name: Lynn
localFacts: Lynn is the largest city in Essex County and one of the oldest colonial settlements in Massachusetts, situated on the Atlantic Ocean just north of Boston.
paintingChallenges: Salt air and ocean wind wear exterior paint faster
Dense multi-family housing with older paint layers
Tight urban lots that complicate ladder and staging access

name: Malden
localFacts: Malden is a densely populated city in Middlesex County just north of Boston, with a large stock of older multi-family homes.
paintingChallenges: Triple-deckers and two-families with many paint layers
Lead-safe rules apply to most pre-1978 housing
Close-set homes make exterior access tight

name: Maynard
localFacts: Maynard sits on the Assabet River about 22 miles west of Boston; much of the Assabet River National Wildlife Refuge lies within the town.
paintingChallenges: Mill-era homes with layered and lead-containing paint
River humidity encourages mildew
Compact downtown lots with limited access

name: Medford
localFacts: Medford is a city in Middlesex County north of Boston and home to Tufts University, whose campus straddles the Medford and Somerville border.
paintingChallenges: Older multi-family and student rental housing
Mystic River humidity in low-lying neighborhoods
Dense streets that complicate exterior staging

name: Melrose
localFacts: Melrose is a city about seven miles north of Boston, known for its large stock of Victorian-era homes, and was first settled in 1628.
paintingChallenges: Victorian homes with detailed trim and multiple colors
Lead paint common on original exteriors
Mature trees keep many facades shaded

name: Norfolk
localFacts: Norfolk, formerly North Wrentham, became an independent town in 1870 and is a largely residential community in Norfolk County.
paintingChallenges: Larger newer homes with extensive exterior trim
Wooded lots with mildew-prone siding
Short exterior season for larger projects

name: Oxford
localFacts: Oxford is a Worcester County town south of Worcester and the birthplace of Clara Barton, founder of the American Red Cross.
paintingChallenges: Older village homes with layered paint
Lake and pond humidity in parts of town
Mix of older and newer construction on the same streets

name: Saugus
localFacts: Saugus is a town in Essex County known as the site of the first integrated iron works in North America, now the Saugus Iron Works National Historic Site.
paintingChallenges: Coastal marsh humidity and salt air
Busy Route 1 corridor with commercial repaint needs
Older homes alongside newer construction

name: Sharon
localFacts: Sharon is a Norfolk County town about 17 miles southwest of Boston, connected to Boston and Providence by commuter rail and known for Lake Massapoag.
paintingChallenges: Lakeside humidity and mildew
Wooded lots that keep siding shaded
Larger colonials with extensive trim

name: Stow
localFacts: Stow is a MetroWest town about 21 miles west of Boston, incorporated in 1683, with orchards, golf courses and conservation land.
paintingChallenges: Rural and wooded lots with damp, shaded walls
Antique homes alongside newer subdivisions
Farm buildings that add to exterior scope

name: Wakefield
localFacts: Wakefield is a Middlesex County town about 12.5 miles north of downtown Boston, centered on Lake Quannapowitt.
paintingChallenges: Lake-adjacent homes face extra humidity
Victorian homes with detailed trim near the center
Mature trees shade many facades

name: Walpole
localFacts: Walpole is about 18 miles south of downtown Boston, first settled in 1659 and incorporated in 1724.
paintingChallenges: Mix of antique center homes and newer neighborhoods
Wooded lots with mildew on shaded siding
Large homes with extensive trim and windows

name: Webster
localFacts: Webster was founded by industrialist Samuel Slater, was home to several early American textile mills, and sits on Lake Chaubunagungamaug, also known as Webster Lake.
paintingChallenges: Lakefront homes with heavy humidity and sun exposure
Mill-era multi-family homes with layered paint
Seasonal lake homes that need maintenance repaints

name: West Boylston
localFacts: West Boylston is a northern suburb of Worcester that includes the village of Oakdale, across the Wachusett Reservoir from the town center.
paintingChallenges: Reservoir-side humidity encourages mildew
Mix of older village homes and newer subdivisions
Shaded wooded lots

name: Wrentham
localFacts: Wrentham is a Norfolk County town between Boston and Providence, known for its lakes and the Wrentham Village Premium Outlets.
paintingChallenges: Lakeside humidity and mildew
Older center homes alongside new construction
Wooded lots that keep siding damp
